title: ffwd-model.json: the manifest of one released model (D-053). The app, helper and CLI read this instead of hard-coded URLs and defaults, and refuse a model whose protocol_version or min_app_version does not match what they were built for.

version.description: MAJOR: prompt, protocol or action schema change. MINOR: new weights, same protocol. PATCH: card or packaging only (D-053).

min_app_version.description: Oldest version of the website, helper or CLI that may load this model, as a semver string. An app older than this refuses the model (fail closed). 1.0.0 for the first release.

protocol_version.description: packages/protocol version the model was trained and evaluated against (training/config.py PROTOCOL_VERSION). An app built for another protocol_version refuses the model.

licence.description: SPDX id of the weights licence.

card.description: Model card; resolved like every file name.

path.description: Relative to the manifest's own URL or folder. Never an absolute URL.

role.description: shipped = the file apps load; evaluated = the file of the headline test results; weights = a file of the merged fp16 Hugging Face model; adapter = LoRA weights for re-merging.

optional.description: true: an extra a consumer may skip (the LoRA adapters). Absent means required. The package still lists it in SHA256SUMS.

add_generation_prompt.description: true: the rendered prompt ends with the assistant turn opener and the empty think block.

canary.description: The WebGPU canary: a fixed prompt whose greedy reply is known. A graphics path whose reply differs is not used. The prompt is not stored: it is re-rendered, byte for byte, from the system prompt (prompt.sha256), the user turn below and the chat template (chat_template.sha256), and its sha256 is rendered_prompt_sha256.

file_sha256.description: The model file this reference was made with (a files[].sha256); it judges no other file.

user_turn.description: Content of the single user message after the system message, verbatim.

kind.description: Count the leading generated ids that equal the expected ones (greedy decoding diverges after the first mismatch). The reply text is tokenised with special tokens not parsed and no BOS.

relpath.description: Relative path: no leading slash, no .. segment, no scheme.
